title: Creatine for the Treatment of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
brief_summary: Creatine is a naturally occurring chemical involved in the production of energy in muscle. Abnormalities in creatine have been linked to the progression of degenerative neuromuscular diseases such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS, or Lou Gehrig's Disease). This study will test whether taking creatine can improve the symptoms of ALS.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria

* Diagnosis of probable or definite ALS
* At least 5 of 10 testable upper extremity muscle groups (shoulder and elbow extensors/flexors and grip) of Medical Research Council (MRC) grade 4 or better
* At least 5 years from onset of symptoms

Exclusion Criteria

* Requires tracheostomy ventilation
* History of renal disease
